newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end sharply lower.

text.p: Swiss shares ended near the day's lows in line with most European markets in the wake of stronger-than-expected data U.S. economic data, a sagging Wall Street and easing SMI futures.

Dealers said that various special situations and technical factors soured sentiment and caused a slump of the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) below the support level of 3,870 points. The volumes were described as below average.
"If Wall Street continues to fall, we will no doubt follow", one trader said.
The SMI was down 32.9 points, or 0.85 percent, to 3,845.3 and the all-share SPI ended .30 points lower at 2,460.78.
A sharp drop in UBS and Swiss Re pressured the entire market. UBS bearer shares plummeted 1.63 percent to 1,209 francs after suffering a loss of more than three percent on Tuesday.
The bank said on Tuesday it would lay off 800 workers and post a loss of 500 million Swiss francs in 1996 due to a one-off extraordinary charge of three billion francs.
Swiss Re shares fell 2.62 percent to 1,414 francs after paying out dividends on its shares.
Major pharmaceuticals Ciba, Sandoz and Roche were under pressure. Roche certificates were 140 francs easier at 9,830. Ciba and Sandoz posted slight losses.
Clariant and Alusuisse ended flat at 443 and 1,017, respectively.

Electrowatt gained five francs to end at 504. Dealers said old rumours were revived that Electrowatt, in which CS Holding has a stake of more than 40 percent, may form an alliance with untility firm Motor Columbus, which is majority-owned by UBS.
Second-tier Ascom jumped more than four percent on takeover rumours. Ascom said the rumours were pure speculation.
